title: Launch Ledger: regional capacity prioritization + Canary Traffic Mesh playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Cross-surface launches (runtime, console, API) lack a single authoritative ledger that ties regional capacity credits, canary routing policy, and stakeholder rotations together. This leads to last-minute capacity collisions, inconsistent canary coverage across regions, and manual comms.

Goal: Create a Launch Ledger playbook plus supporting automation that: 1) records and enforces regional capacity credit allocations per release train, 2) generates canary traffic mesh policies for runtime to ensure even coverage and safe fallbacks, and 3) surfaces a compact console dashboard and weekly stakeholder rota to eliminate manual coordination. Deliverables are a playbook doc, a console dashboard widget prototype, runtime routing integration design, and a validation simulation harness.

Why now: Dedicated and Private customers are increasingly sensitive to capacity reservations and predictable SLAs. Recent incidents where two product trains consumed the same reserved capacity highlighted the need for ledgered reservations and guardrails.

Success metrics:
- Reduce cross-train capacity collisions to 0 in Q2 launches (from 3 incidents last 6 months).
- Canary coverage parity: >= 90% of canary traffic routed through the mesh in each active region during staged rollouts.
- Time-to-decision for launch cutover reduced by 40% (measured from 'go/no-go' request to decision).
acceptance_criteria: A documented Launch Ledger playbook covering registration, reservation, and dispute resolution
Console widget prototype that shows per-train capacity credits, active canaries, and owner rota
Runtime routing config schema and a proof-of-concept that programmatically generates canary traffic meshes for a given train
Simulation harness that runs 500 synthetic launch scenarios and verifies no double-booked capacity in >95% of runs
Runbook and stakeholder on-call rota exported as calendar invites and available from the dashboard
Post-launch metrics pipeline shows capacity usage and canary SLI trends for 30 days

stakeholders: Eng leads: Diego Ramirez (Runtime), Priya Nair (Console), Omar Khalid (Orchestration)
risks: Runtime integration complexity: tying ledger reservations to live routing could introduce throttles if schema mismatches occur
Stakeholder buy-in: teams may resist ticketed reservations vs informal slack agreements
Automation edge-cases: calendar/rota automation must respect org holidays and regional on-call patterns
Data fidelity: capacity credits must be reconciled with Dedicated contracts to avoid over-commitment
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): 2-week discovery with Runtime/Console/SRE to finalize ledger model
Phase 1 (POC): Implement ledger API (read/write), canary-mesh generator, and console mock
Phase 2 (Pilot): Run ledger+mesh on a non-customer-visible runtime release train for 2 waves
Phase 3 (Expand): Enable for one hosted API and one Dedicated customer train concurrently
Fallback: If simulation identifies >2 conflict classes, revert to manual reservation gating and extend pilot
